title: Keep an easy native law while rejecting total-order truncation
statement: At H=0,gamma=T=1 and fixed rational eta>0, the native law is P_b(x)=2^-n product_i(1+b x_i), b=eta/(2+eta)(1-exp(-(1+eta/2)))>0. Absolute subset mass is (1+b)^n. For normalized signed total-order truncation q_L with L=o(n), the typical magnetization event has P_b mass->1 but |q_L| mass->0. Thus half||P_b-q_L||1>=1-o(1), and the actual accepted positive-prefix converter Q_L<=q_L_plus has TV(P_b,Q_L)->1. The original law remains easy by resumming its singleton factors.
